subject: biochemistry
title: Fatty acid beta-oxidation, carnitine shuttle and ketogenesis

steps.tx: Long-chain fatty acids require activation to fatty acyl-CoA by thiokinase in the cytosol before mitochondrial translocation. Transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane is mediated by the **carnitine shuttle**. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase-one converts acyl-CoA to acylcarnitine at the outer membrane, inhibited allosterically by malonyl-CoA during active lipogenesis. A translocase shuttles acylcarnitine inside, where carnitine palmitoyltransferase-two regenerates matrix acyl-CoA.
steps.say: Long-chain fatty acids require activation to acyl-CoA before mitochondrial entry via the carnitine shuttle. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase-one converts acyl-CoA to acylcarnitine, inhibited by malonyl-CoA during lipogenesis. A translocase carries acylcarnitine across the inner membrane, where carnitine palmitoyltransferase-two regenerates mitochondrial acyl-CoA.

rows: Replaces CoA with carnitine; rate-limiting step
Antiporter swapping acylcarnitine for free carnitine
Catalyzes initial dehydrogenation step yielding FADH2

steps.tx: Mitochondrial **beta-oxidation** proceeds through a four-step recurring spiral: oxidation by acyl-CoA dehydrogenase yielding FADH2; hydration by enoyl-CoA hydratase; oxidation by hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase yielding NADH; and thiolytic cleavage by thiolase yielding acetyl-CoA and a fatty acyl-CoA shortened by two carbons. Each complete cycle of palmitate (sixteen carbons) produces eight acetyl-CoA, seven FADH2 and seven NADH, yielding over one hundred ATP.
steps.say: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation proceeds through four recurring steps: oxidation yielding FADH2, hydration, second oxidation yielding NADH, and thiolytic cleavage yielding acetyl-CoA and an acyl-CoA shortened by two carbons. Palmitate oxidation yields eight acetyl-CoA, seven FADH2 and seven NADH, generating over one hundred ATP.

steps.tx: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is the most common inborn error of lipid catabolism. An inability to break down fatty acids with six to twelve carbons results in severe **hypoketotic hypoglycemia** during prolonged fasting or intercurrent viral illness. Glycogen reserves become depleted while gluconeogenesis fails due to lack of acetyl-CoA activation of pyruvate carboxylase, accumulating dicarboxylic acids and octanoylcarnitine.
steps.say: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is the most common inborn lipid disorder. An inability to break down medium-chain fats causes severe hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting. Gluconeogenesis fails due to lack of acetyl-CoA, leading to dicarboxylic acidemia and lethargy.

steps.tx: During starvation or untreated diabetic ketoacidosis, massive adipose lipolysis floods the liver with fatty acids. Excessive acetyl-CoA saturates the tricarboxylic acid cycle and is diverted into hepatic **ketogenesis**. Mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase converts acetyl-CoA to acetoacetate, beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetone. Extrahepatic tissues convert acetoacetate to acetyl-CoA using thiophorase. The liver cannot utilize ketone bodies because it completely lacks thiophorase.
steps.say: During starvation or diabetic ketoacidosis, excessive acetyl-CoA saturates the Krebs cycle and drives hepatic ketogenesis. Mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase synthesizes acetoacetate, beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetone. Extrahepatic tissues use acetoacetate via thiophorase. The liver cannot use ketones because it lacks thiophorase.
